experiments.why: A plain converted invoice outside any schedule already carries the estimate id, so no link may be stamped.
Job invoices that carry a different estimate id leave the link free for the first milestone.
A unique violation on the (schedule_id, milestone_index) index is the duplicate-milestone case.
A unique violation on the estimate index must not be mistaken for an already minted milestone.
A 50/50 deposit/balance split of an odd total must round the deposit and give the balance the exact rest.
A non-integer total must be rejected.
Percents summing to exactly 10000 bps with one remainder must be accepted.

source.quote: mints the on_completion balance milestone on completion

obligations.statement: For a job whose 50/50 deposit/balance schedule already has its deposit minted, mintCompletionMilestones returns exactly one new invoice: the on_completion balance for that schedule, milestone index 1, totalling the remaining 50%.

source.quote: is idempotent — a second completion mints nothing new

obligations.statement: Calling mintCompletionMilestones a second time for the same job mints nothing new: it returns an empty list and the job keeps the same invoices.

source.quote: bills the on_completion balance when the deposit already links the estimate

obligations.statement: When the schedule's own deposit invoice already carries the estimate id, mintCompletionMilestones still mints the on_completion balance as one invoice for milestone index 1 with the remaining amount.
When the schedule's own deposit invoice already carries the estimate id, the balance invoice minted by mintCompletionMilestones has no estimateId.
When the schedule has an estimate and its deposit invoice does not carry it, the balance invoice minted by mintCompletionMilestones carries the schedule's estimateId.

If creating a milestone invoice fails with the (schedule_id, milestone_index) unique violation, mintCompletionMilestones treats that milestone as already minted: it returns no invoice for it and does not throw.

source.quote: True only for the (schedule_id, milestone_index) duplicate-key violation.

obligations.statement: isDuplicateMilestoneError returns true for a unique violation on the (schedule_id, milestone_index) index uniq_invoices_schedule_milestone and false for any other error, including a unique violation on another index such as uq_invoices_estimate.

source.quote: Returns the estimateId to stamp on the next milestone

obligations.statement: milestoneEstimateLink returns the given estimateId when no invoice on the job carries that estimate id yet.

source.quote: invoice, or undefined when an invoice on the job already holds the link.

obligations.statement: milestoneEstimateLink returns undefined when an invoice on the job already carries the estimate id.

source.quote: the remainder absorbs rounding so the sum equals the total exactly

obligations.statement: splitMilestones gives each percent milestone its rounded share and the remainder milestone the rest, so the amounts always sum to the total exactly (3333 bps of 10000 cents is 3333 and the remainder takes 6667).

source.quote: throws when fixed amounts exceed the total

obligations.statement: splitMilestones throws when the fixed (flat and percent) portions exceed the total, such as a 15000-cent flat milestone against a 10000-cent total.

source.quote: throws on a negative or non-integer total

obligations.statement: splitMilestones throws for a negative or non-integer total.
validateMilestones reports an exactly one 'remainder' error for a list with no remainder milestone or with two of them.

source.quote: rejects percent milestones that sum past 100% (total-independent)

obligations.statement: validateMilestones reports an error when percent milestones sum past 10000 bps, whatever the total, and accepts percents that sum to exactly 10000 bps.

source.quote: refuses to build a schedule with invalid milestones

obligations.statement: buildInvoiceSchedule throws instead of building a schedule whose milestones are invalid, such as a list with no remainder milestone.
